what_it_does: Helix solves a fundamental problem in tensor computation: when a neural network receives inputs of different sizes, the computational kernel (the optimized code that performs calculations) must be recompiled for each new size. Current approaches collect samples of input shapes to guide optimization, which is expensive and performs poorly on unseen shapes. Helix uses shape-agnostic compilation that works for any input size without needing samples.
method_in_detail: Helix decomposes tensor operations hierarchically across three architectural levels: high-level (algorithmic strategy), mid-level (loop and memory organization), and low-level (hardware-specific optimizations). It uses a bidirectional strategy combining top-down abstraction (understanding what computations need) and bottom-up kernel construction (building optimized code from hardware capabilities). The system includes a hybrid analyzer that does profiling at the lowest levels where measurement is accurate, and mathematical modeling at higher levels where patterns are more predictable.
